A transformer is a type of electrical equipment that is used to change the voltage of an alternating current (AC) electrical supply. It consists of two or more coils of wire, known as the primary and secondary windings, which are wrapped around a common magnetic core. When an AC current flows through the primary winding, it creates a magnetic field that induces a voltage in the secondary winding. The voltage in the secondary winding can be either AC or DC, depending on the design of the transformer.

The transformer is a fundamental device in the operation of many electrical systems, including power grids and electronic circuits. It is used to step up or step down the voltage of an electrical supply, to match the voltage and current requirements of different devices and appliances. Transformers can also be used to isolate electrical circuits from each other, by preventing direct electrical contact between the primary and secondary windings.

Transformers are designed according to various ratings, including voltage rating, current rating, and power rating. They can be made in various sizes and shapes, and can be used in a wide range of applications, including in homes, businesses, and industries.
